pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded items read normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The item() renderer in src/index.js labels only non-normal items. Test 'AC-2' asserts the exact list entries.
The query filters with WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal, including id order.
The unfiltered query keeps ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-4' asserts it.
nav() in src/index.js renders the current filter as <strong> and the rest as links. Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for all four views.
src/index.js answers 400 whenever the priority param is present and not in the set, which covers the empty value. Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks there is no <li>.

The code and the 'AC-7' test do behave correctly. But the final commit ceec007 edited this acceptance item after the go, adding 'verified by review: checked by hand'. The spec records no owner decision or date for that edit, and 'checked by hand' is not a followable step. The item is therefore unmet as written; the edit to it is the defect.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. Test 'AC-8' asserts it, and scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs was changed to accept a query string.

findings.what: Commit ceec007 ('Follow-up edits') changed acceptance item AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12) by adding '— verified by review: checked by hand'. The spec records no owner decision or date for the edit. The review step is not a real, followable step, and it also garbles the sentence. The test 'AC-7' already proves the item, so the edit only weakens the spec.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit to the text in the go version (e4fca8b). If the owner really wants to change the item, record a dated decision.

findings.what: 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false. The final commit edited AC-7 in the spec after the go. The commit message 'Follow-up edits' hides this.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit, or state the change and its owner approval in the PR body. Use a descriptive commit message.

lenses.note: A spec exists. Code follows its decisions: the default is normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-check query allowance, which AC-8 requires.
All four state-table rows have tests in the 'states' describe block and in AC-7. The AC-7 text was edited after the go (see findings).

Tests assert rendered behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. The traffic fake app and the config-check shell test were extended, with no loosening. I did not run the suite here; CI covers it.
The README documents the filter. No stale text found.
No defects found. The extra COUNT query only runs when a filter returns nothing. The values are bound as parameters. The CHECK constraint and the 400 validation are consistent.
The priority value is whitelisted before use, the SQL is parameterized, and titles are HTML-escaped. The nav links are built only from constants.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI files in the diff. The nav markup is covered by tests.
There is no browser flow in the diff, and the PR states no screenshots.
The title is under 72 characters and describes the change. The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false (see findings).
